newsitem.title: USA: Ford cuts car loan rates to 1.9 percent.
newsitem.headline: Ford cuts car loan rates to 1.9 percent.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said Friday it slashed financing rates on its best-selling car models to 1.9 percent and also is offering reduced-rate loans on its Ford Explorer and Mercury Mountaineer sport utility vehicles.

The 1.9 percent interest rates are being offered by Ford Motor Credit Co on 48-month loans on the Ford Taurus, Escort, Contour and Thunderbird and the Mercury Sable, Tracer, Mystique and Cougar. The reduced rates are effective between May 3 and July 7, Ford said.
Previously, Ford Credit offered 7.9 percent loans on Contour and Mystique and 4.8 percent loans on the other cars.
Cash incentives on the cars, offered in lieu of the cheaper financing, remain unchanged.

Ford said that, although it toppled General Motors Corp from its position as the biggest seller of sport utility vehicles, it is offering the first-ever retail financing incentives on its Explorer and Mountaineer.
The Ford Credit financing rates of 4.8 percent on 48-month loans on the vehicles and 5.9 percent on 49-60 month loans, are available from May 8 through June 2.

Previously, Ford had offered only leasing incentives on the compact sport utility vehicles. Combined Explorer and Mountaineer sales for the first four months of 1997 are down 4.5 percent from a year earlier to 132,792 units.

"We know that, all things being equal, compact utility customers prefer Explorer, as evidenced by the fact that it is outselling its nearest competitor by 47 percent," Ford group vice president of sales and marketing Robert Rewey said in a statement.
"These reduced APRs enable our dealers to compete on an equal basis."

Ford said that, through the first four months of 1997, its three sport utility models, which also include the new full-size Expedition, have outsold GM's eight models 200,400 to 199,669. A year ago, GM sold 209,210 sport utility vehicles compared with Ford's to 154,412.
